utterances.text: Yes. I got to know him under his real name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Branko Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you describe for us when it was you first met Marko Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I think it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how long after you initially met him did you learn his real name was Brano Popovic [sic]?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I became acquainted with him under his real name, Branko Popovic, and I knew that when the clash broke out in Zvornik he started to introduce himself using another name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he ever indicate to you why he would use an alias around the time that the hostilities broke out in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We never discussed that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did he say his real name is Branko or Brano? Let me clarify this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it's Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, when he was in the -- the Zvornik area, where would he stay?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Before the conflict, that was the Hotel Jezero, situated in Mali Zvornik. And once the conflict began, I think he used some flats in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge regarding whether he met with members of the Yugoslav People's Army at that hotel before and during the early stages of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I didn't personally see him meet with any people, but he did inform the headquarters and staff that he had good contacts with the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he indicate to the headquarters which particular members or the names of the particular members of the JNA he had good contacts with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: He mentioned the commander of the Tuzla Corps, for example, General Savo Jankovic, and Lieutenant-Colonel or Colonel Dubajic, and some other men whose names I can't remember exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us with as much precision as you are able when it was -- or what period of time he was referring to when he said he had good contacts with General Jankovic, the commander of the Tuzla Corps?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: That was the period six months before the war conflicts broke out in Zvornik, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when in your view did the war conflicts break out in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, round about -- from the 6th to the 9th of April, between those dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know a person or did Mr. Pavlovic ever reveal to you contacts he may have had with a person by the name of Dragan Suka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, he did have contacts with him, with the person you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who is or who was Dragan Suka at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: As I worked in the police, I knew that he was a member of the state security in Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held in the state security service of Loznica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't know exactly how they were set up organisationally speaking, but I think he was the chief for the municipality or perhaps for the neighbouring municipalities as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did Mr. Pavlovic indicate to you with what frequency and over what period of time he had these contacts with Mr. Suka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We didn't discuss that very much, but I saw them together. I knew that they had been together a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You have testified that you met or were introduced to Mr. Pavlovic by a person by the name of Rade Kostic. Can you describe for the Chamber what you know about the relationship between Marko Pavlovic and Rade Kostic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, what I know is this: Pavlovic was included in the war conflicts, involved in them, the ones that took place in Croatia, in the Baranja region of Croatia, and also that - to a certain extent that was the impression I gained - he listened to Rade Kostic. He seemed to be his assistant in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: For what -- or over what period of time did you have contact with Marko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: That was in the period -- in a four or five-month period prior to the conflict in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did you continue to have contact with him after the conflict began?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I did, for a time, while I was a member of the Crisis Staff. And afterwards I worked in the economy, but Zvornik is a small place and we all had contacts more or less.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give us an estimate of the entire period of time over which you've known Marko Pavlovic? Is it a year, less than a year? Or can you give us a precise answer to that question?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand the question fully, but I've known him since 1991. I knew him during 1992 as well. He left the area, I think it was in July of 1992, and I saw him twice after that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Drawing your attention to 1991 and 1992. Based upon your observations of him and the activities he was engaged in, did you form an opinion with respect to who he worked for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, according to what I knew, his best contacts were with the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever learn or -- I'm not asking you about his contacts, but he himself. Did you ever learn or did you have an opinion about who he himself worked with or any organisation he was associated with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were you ever present when Mr. Pavlovic made a phone call after which something significant arrived in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Pavlovic, in front of the whole Crisis Staff, called up some telephone numbers that I didn't know, weren't familiar to me, and he contacted officers from the JNA. And I know that the result of all that was the arrival of the -- of some logistical goods necessary for the Territorial Defence of Zvornik at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you be more precise? What exactly were these logistical goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, we lacked ammunition and weapons, uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time that Mr. Pavlovic made this phone call in front of the Crisis Staff, did he represent to the people present that he would be able to secure the logistical equipment, including ammunition and weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. That was quite clear from his conversations. And it instilled respect within the Crisis Staff that we had the right man and the right sort of support.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What period of time elapsed between the time he made this phone call and the arrival of the first of these shipments of logistical goods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, it was all done within the space of 24 to 48 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you give the Chamber some sense of the quantity of goods that arrived by perhaps describing the number of -- of trucks or, if you know, the specific quantities of goods, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I really can't say. I wasn't involved with those affairs, so I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And if you would, please give us your most precise recollection about when this occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: This occurred in the period between the 6th of April, 1992 up until the 20th of April, 1992. And I don't know how this was organised after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd like to now draw your attention to this Rade Kostic that you've mentioned. Can you please describe who he is and the circumstances under which you know him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: He was born right near Zvornik, in Serbia, in the municipality of Mali Zvornik. And I knew him privately, while he was the commander of the police station in Darda in Croatia. And then later on I know that he took up some official post in the Ministry of the Interior in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your knowledge regarding the post he took up in the Serbian Ministry of the Interior, is that because he told you that that's where he worked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: He just said he worked in the Ministry of the Interior. He didn't tell me any details about it. But I knew that he worked in the state security service. What post he held and what his assignments were, he never spoke much about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is he alive today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No. Rade Kostic died in 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you attend his funeral?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to list some of the more prominent people who attended Rade Kostic's funeral.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, amongst the people I knew, there was Mr. Stanisic, Bogdanovic, Arkan. There were many people from political circles and cultural circles as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at the monitor in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And I'd ask the usher maybe to assist in setting the monitor so he can see the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This is a still from Prosecution Exhibit 390, tab 18 -- sorry, tab 6. It's a video. This is just one still. Do you recognise the memorial that's depicted there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I do. That is the memorial of the late Rade Kostic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now ask you about a person by the name of Brano Grujic. Do you know him? And please tell us the circumstances under which you know him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, I do know Grujic. Grujic worked in Zvornik. And as Zvornik is a small town, we know each other and we've known each other since we were children almost.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My apologies. There's one additional question I'd like to ask you with respect to Rade Kostic: Did you and Rade Kostic ever have a conversation regarding Arkan? And if so, can you summarise what that conversation was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: When the war conflicts broke out in Bijeljina, Kostic phoned me up and told me that I was to go to Bijeljina and to report there to the Dom Kultura or cultural centre in Bijeljina in order to secure logistical support for his unit which was to cross into Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time that Mr. Kostic gave you these instructions, do you know whether he was acting in his professional capacity or his official capacity as a member of the state security service or in his personal capacity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I'm not quite clear on that, because generally I had private relationships with Kostic, and I had very little contact on an official level with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, once again, drawing your attention to Mr. Grujic. Did Mr. Grujic ever discuss with you his relationship with Mr. Jovica Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: He told me that he had been with him only once at a meeting in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he indicate when that meeting was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I think it was in 1992, but I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, can you tell the Chamber regarding Mr. Grujic's relationship to the Bosnian Serb leadership of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, Grujic was the president of the Serbian Democratic Party, since its inception in Zvornik, right up until almost 1995. So by virtue of his office, he had contacts with the leadership at Pale. However, I think that the popular deputy Mijatovic had more contacts than he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Mr. Mijatovic is the next person I'd ask you to speak about. Can you describe what his position and role was in Zvornik. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Jovo Mijatovic was a member of parliament, a deputy elected at the elections in 1991, and he was a national deputy right up until 1995. That's the office he occupied. And pursuant to the decision of setting up municipalities according to B variant, he was president of the parallel Municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you aware of any meeting that he attended with Arkan in the Hotel Jezero in Mali Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. In those days, the Serbian Democratic Party's political aim was to try and come to an agreement with the SDA as representing the Muslim people. And as the Crisis Staff, we sent Mijatovic and Ivanovic to attend a meeting in Mali Zvornik because the situation was already such that the Muslims couldn't reach our headquarters in Karakaj and we couldn't reach their headquarters in Zvornik. So we sent them to negotiate at the Jezero Hotel in Mali Zvornik for us to try to come to some sort of agreement if possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was an agreement reached at that meeting between the local leadership of the SDS and the SDA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We tried to reach an agreement, but after the recognition of Bosnia and Herzegovina it was virtually not possible to come to any kind of agreement. But we tried at the local level to reach an agreement, but the meeting in Mali Zvornik was interrupted. Mijatovic and Ivanovic told us later on at the staff, with the incursion of Arkan and his officers who beat up all the negotiators. In fact, the Serbs more than the Muslims. And that is how that meeting came to an end.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why were the Serb negotiators beaten by Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Probably to instil fear in the Bosniak, Muslim side. And later on he came to the headquarters at the Alhos facilities in Karakaj and he threatened us. He started shouting, "Who gave you the authority to sell out and divide and with the Muslims Serbian land?" And he started slapping people.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What became of the agreement that had been reached between the SDS leadership and the SDA leadership?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You said to us before Arkan's arrival that an agreement had been reached between the respective leaderships of the two parties. What became of that agreement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We tried to reach some sort of an agreement at the local level, not to do anything stupid and to wait for a solution for Bosnia as a whole. However, that agreement fell through and Arkan prohibited the Crisis Staff from having any contact with the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could I ask you in just a sentence or two, just to describe in very general terms in your view what was the relationship between the Serb community and the Muslim community prior to the outbreak of tensions between the two?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Ever since the elections, when the nationalist parties won, relations became more complicated and they became very tense, and this tension culminated with the recognition of the independence of Bosnia, and this was a climax after which it was not possible to reconcile the peoples of Bosnia again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 2. I'd ask you: Do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please summarise what that document is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: This is a decision banning the sale of real estate, issued by the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik on the 15th of March, 1992, prohibiting the Serbs from selling their land and property to non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to read the sentence that begins on the top of the right-hand page.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: "Privately owned real estates by ethnic Serbs cannot be traded to other ethnic groups on the territory of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was this order or decision observed and enforced?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, this decision was issued by the parallel Serbian Municipality of Zvornik, but I don't think that there was any sale of Serbian land because this was issued only some 15 or 20 days before the war began.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you aware of a -- a fax that was sent by Momcilo Mandic around the 4th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. At the time, I was the commander of the police station and we did receive a dispatch.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe in substance what was in that fax.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The substance was, of that fax, was reference to the Cutilheiro Plan, when Izetbegovic, Karadzic, the leadership, agreed on some sort of a division of Bosnia, and then the fax emanated from that plan, ordering all members of Serb ethnicity in the police to cross over and join the Serbian police, which was organised on the basis of a table that he had drawn up, and we were told that this would be financed with the funds of the Serbian Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina, as it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At the time you saw this fax, did it -- did it indicate something to you or did you believe it was an indication of something to come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The situation was already extremely complicated and tense to a high degree among the ethnicities, so actually this marked the final division of the MUP. And it's like glass; once you break it, you can't put it together again.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened to the Serb members of the local Zvornik MUP after receipt of this fax?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I was the leading representative of the Serbs in the police, and they all got together in my office and vice versa, with the chief of police -- in the chief of police's office all the Muslims got together. And that was when the SUP was divided up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did the Serb members of the -- of the Serbian police go?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We went together with the Crisis Staff to the Alhos building in Karakaj, which was about 5 kilometres from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where was the headquarters of the Serb part of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: At first, both the TO and the Crisis Staff and the police were all together in the Alhos building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now show you Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 3 and ask you to take a look at it and ask you do you recognise it.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. That is the dispatch we received on the 31st of March, 1992, signed by the Assistant Minister of Internal Affairs, Mr. Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention to the influx of arms, weapons, and ammunition into the Zvornik municipality. I would ask you to give us a brief summary at this point on did arms come into the municipality and in general terms how did they arrive at the municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, weapons did come into the municipality. There were many different ways, many different channels, and the conflict was visible virtually everywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were some of the means that were used to arm people, did you consider them legal means to arm people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, in addition to legal arming, the Muslims mostly purchased weapons from Croatia; whereas, we received them through the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: The arms that you received through the JNA, can you describe in greater detail how they were received -- requested and received by people in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I do know that in Zvornik municipality there were several channels. The Muslims didn't join the JNA, and then when the Serbs filled in the vacancies, they received weapons. But that was in order. That was regular. However, talking about irregular, secret ways, we were frightened, being the minority in that area. We went to see the president of the assembly commission for relations with Serbs outside Serbia, as the commission was called in those days, and we requested aid in weapons because we felt we were in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who was the president of that assembly commission?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Mr. Pudarevic [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know his first name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Radmilo Bogdanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what happened after meeting with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We presented our positions, describing the situation we were in. We asked him to help us. And he told me that in the next ten days or so, Kostic would call me to organise this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did Mr. Kostic call you after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Six or seven days later, I was called up by him and given instructions what should be done, and these were more or less as follows: We drove a truck to the parking lot of the Belgrade fairgrounds. We left it there full of fuel, and the keys were in the vehicle. And then in the afternoon we would come back and find that same truck loaded, usually with wheat, flour, and it would have a fictitious invoice because this was still within the framework of a single state. There was no control at the borders. We would drive this back to Zvornik, and then we would count the quantity of weapons, and the Crisis Staff would agree to distribute it among Serbian villages on the basis of an acceptment of the degree of danger they were in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How many times did you personally participate in the importation of arms into Zvornik in this manner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I participated twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you estimate for us the quantity of weapons that were imported on both of those occasions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I think on those two occasions, between 200 and 300 pieces of weapons. Between 200 and 300 pieces.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And with as much precision as you're able, can you tell us when these two events occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I participated, I think, at the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, would that be a convenient place?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn now. Witness B-024, we're going to adjourn now for 20 minutes. Would you remember in this adjournment and any others there may be during your evidence not to speak to anybody about it until it's over, and that does include the members of the Prosecution team. We'll adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, I want to ask you a few more questions about the importation of arms into Zvornik. Are you aware of any participation that Brano Grujic had in this activity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I am aware of the first quantity that arrived. It arrived through a contact of his.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please tell us when that shipment arrived.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly, but it was in the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you tell us what was involved in that shipment and from where did it come.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Grujic told me that this was organised with some people in Serbia, and there were about 30 pieces of automatic weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a person -- a colonel in the Yugoslav People's Army by the name of Colonel Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if any, involvement did he have in the importation of weapons into Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe what role he played or how he was involved.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I think that a member of the Crisis Staff had close relations with him, and he sent a certain quantity. I think he was somewhere in Romanija. I don't remember exactly which unit. And he sent a certain quantity of weapons from there, which again through the Crisis Staff and the SDS in Zvornik was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What is the earliest point in time that you're aware of that weapons were being imported illegally into Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The first shipment that was brought by Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that's the one, you said, in the autumn of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, of the -- all of the weapons that were brought into Zvornik in these various manners that you've described, are you able to estimate the percentage of the total number of weapons that belonged to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, most of it was from the depots and warehouses of the JNA. Maybe -- at least two-thirds of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask you to now turn your attention to the distribution of these weapons. Can you describe what happened to these weapons once they were brought into the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It would be located in one of the ethnically pure Serb local communes, and then the Crisis Staff would sit down and agree on the distribution, on the basis of their assessment of the degree of danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And once this assessment was made, what would physically happen to the weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, then from these centres where the weapons were stored, individuals of local communes would come, usually SDS leaders. They would pick up certain quantities and then distribute them in their own local communes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Would they have to sign documents or receipts indicating that they received a certain number of weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: In those days, we kept records, and everyone did have to sign.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when is the earliest point in time that you are personally aware of weapons were -- weapons were distributed in the fashion you've described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: In the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, if I might turn your attention to the issue of media coverage. Can I ask you to characterise the media coverage that you observed coming from Belgrade in the autumn of 1991 and early 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The media, as there was a war on already in Croatia and the structure of the population was well known in Bosnia, and the media were divided. They routed each for his own side.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you aware of any media coverage that you observed coming from Serbia regarding Zvornik that you knew to be materially false?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So as far as you're concerned, the events in Zvornik as depicted on Serb media were accurately depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Do you mean at the beginning of the war or before the beginning of the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Let's take both of those separately. Prior to the war's start, did you -- the events from Zvornik that you saw on TV, were they accurately depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Up until the beginning of the conflict, Zvornik was not very much in the focus of attention of the media. At least, I don't remember it being focussed on by the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Then allow me to draw your attention to after the war started, the events that concerned Zvornik, were they accurately depicted in the Serb media in your view?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The media reported regularly about all events on the battlefronts, and in those days there were things that were spoken of and there were things that the media did not report about but that happened on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give us an example of one of those events as it pertained to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: For instance, I know that the Belgrade media never reported on prisons for Muslims in Zvornik, for instance, that there were killings of civilians, though these things were common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to now draw your attention once again to the autumn of 1991. Did there come a time when you attended an SDS rally in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I did attend a large meeting of the SDS at the Holiday Inn in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was that rally -- when was that meeting held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I think it was around the 19th or 20th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And can you please identify any of the prominent members of the SDS leadership that were present during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I do remember that there was Karadzic, Krajisnik, Mrs. Plavsic, and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of that meeting, was there anything distributed to some of the people present at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. To the presidents of municipal boards of the party a document was distributed, roughly indicating how we should behave should a crisis occur in the future.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What did you and others refer to this document as? Did this document have a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It did have a lengthy title, but we called it Plan A and Plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Plan A -- was it called Plan A or Plan B because it had two scenarios, either Plan A or Plan B?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Plan A was the plan for the municipalities in which the Serbs had a majority, and Plan B was for the municipalities in which the Serbs were in the minority.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were the presidents of the Crisis Staff instructed to implement Plan A or Plan B based upon the ethnic make-up of their respective municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 434, tab 4. It was used with an earlier witness. I believe copies have been provided to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is the document you asked me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And is that the document the presidents of the Crisis Staff received in December of 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Another witness has gone through the plan and discussed it in some detail, but could I ask you to describe for us, was this plan implemented in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And which variation of the plan was implemented in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We were a municipality in which the Serbs were in the minority, which meant Plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After December of 1991, with what frequency did the -- the members of the SDS and the Crisis Staff meet in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for a clarification, that was Prosecutor's Exhibit 434, tab 3, not tab 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honours, Ms. Wee informs me that at that time it was just marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It was marked for identification, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So based upon this witness's testimony, we would be tendered it into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. It's admissible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: My question to you is: After the receipt of this document, with what frequency was it referred to with respect to instructions of how to implement it in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Among other things, the plan envisaged duty service every day in the party and daily meetings of the Crisis Staff, so that we discussed this almost on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, aside from Zvornik, are you aware that the plan was used and applied in other municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. It was distributed to all the municipalities in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the plan envisage the creation of a Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, the plan envisaged a Crisis Staff at the level of Bosnia and Herzegovina and also Crisis Staffs at municipal levels, and these instructions also explicitly stated who would be members ex officio as members of the party, which members would become members of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who was head of the Crisis Staff in the Bosnian-wide level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: At the level of Bosnia, I don't know. But in Zvornik it was Mr. Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Do you know who was head of the Crisis Staff at the regional level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. I think it was when Semberija and Majevica were formed as Serbian Autonomous Regions pursuant to these instructions that it was Djuro Jeserovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the name for the benefit of the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Djojo Arsenovic, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to tell us in a little greater detail about the Crisis Staff of Zvornik. First, can I ask you to tell us how many members -- or how many people made up the Crisis Staff of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I know that this varied in our case, because clearly the plan was implemented in different ways in different municipalities. But it varied between 10 and 15 members of the Crisis Staff, among whom 7 or 8 were always members, permanent members.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: In the Zvornik Crisis Staff, can you tell me the names of the -- the most or more prominent people in the Zvornik Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: There were Grujic certainly, Stevan Ivanovic, Jovo Ivanovic, Jovo Mijatovic, Stevo Radic, myself, and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And did the Crisis Staff meet on a daily basis during the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Not every day, but very frequently.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give the Chamber some sense of the types of business that were discussed during Crisis Staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, generally, they discussed the political and security situation in our municipality and also measures to implement the plan, how far we had got there, according to Plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After discussions in Zvornik about how far the plan had been implemented, would the results of that discussion be passed upward to the republican level?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, according to this plan, it was our duty to inform any major occurrences taking place with respect to security. And I didn't -- I wasn't in charge of the contacts towards the republican staffs and headquarters, so I don't know how that evolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time in April when the Crisis Staff was reformed into a temporary government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And would it be fair to say that all members of the Crisis Staff were of Serb ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. I think that in Zvornik there was a specific feature according to which at the beginning a member of the Crisis Staff and temporary provisional government was a leading cardiologist from Zvornik, and his name was Mr. Muhamed Jelkic. I did see him at the headquarters, and I think he was there because he was forced to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 4. And I'd simply ask you: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what is this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: These are the conclusions of the 22nd of December, 1991. Amongst others, we have the names of people here elected to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned Mrs. Plavsic, Biljana Plavsic, in your testimony earlier. Was there a time in the spring of 1992 that you met her in Zvornik municipality?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. In fact, at the Crisis Staff in the Alhos factory building in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when precisely did you meet her?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, it was actually twice. The first time, one or two days prior to the conflict in Zvornik; and the second time, two or three days after the conflict in Zvornik had broken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: At this point in time, I'd like to just focus on the -- the meeting prior to the conflict breaking out. And I'd ask you to describe for us who else was present at the Crisis Staff at that time.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, most of the Crisis Staff members were present. There was Pejic, Arkan's officer. We had the rank of major, and we called him Major Pejic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many people all together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, in the whole headquarters, there were a lot of people. But where she sat in that office, perhaps seven or eight persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And were you present during the discussions that took place in that office?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, in part.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please summarise for us the discussions that took place while you were present in that office.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We informed them of the political and security situation in Zvornik, and she was interested in whether we had carried out all the preparatory steps according to Plan B for crisis situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, was she told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, we wanted to congratulate ourselves and say that we had in fact carried out all the preparations pursuant to Plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what, if anything, did she say after hearing that report?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The situation was rather one of confusion. She was still in the Presidency in Sarajevo together with the other Presidency members, and she said that we'd keep in contact -- be in contact and follow the developments of the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention once again to the meeting at Hotel Jezero that you described earlier for us, that you described as Arkan as being present. Can I ask you to describe all of the other people who you are aware were present at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: At the Jezero Hotel, there were two meetings that were held. One was the one I attended, where an attempt was made to reach an agreement with the Muslims. And representing the Serb side was Grujic, Radic, Ivanovic, both Ivanovics, I myself, and an officer, a JNA officer. He was a captain at the time, and his name was Dragan Obrenovic. On the Bosnian side, the Bosniak side, the Muslim side, there was the president of the SDA as well as the head of SUP, Osman Mustafic was his name, and then the head of the TO, Alija Kapidzic, there was Izet Mehinagic, and perhaps a few others, I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Was Marko Pavlovic present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No, Marko Pavlovic was not present at that particular meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I want to ask you some questions with respect to Arkan. Did you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. have dealings with Arkan prior to him coming to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No, I did not. I heard of him just a few days from the newspapers reporting on the events that had taken place in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I ask you to tell us what you know about Arkan's presence in Bijeljina, how that came to be, if you do know.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that really. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time during the takeover of Bijeljina that you went to Bijeljina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. I went to have a meeting with Arkan at the Dom Kultura or cultural centre in Bijeljina, and the conflicts were already ongoing there. There was shooting in town. I went to the cultural centre and waited there for about an hour or an hour and a half, at which point he turned up.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say "he," are you referring to Arkan himself?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who did he arrive with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, he arrived with a group of his combatants. And I saw that where there was a luncheon given for those combatants in the cultural centre, everybody suddenly got to their feet and stood to attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How did you know or -- sorry, how did you know to go to the Dom culture centre to meet Arkan? Who told you that's where you would meet him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I have already said that Kostic told me this over the phone. He told me to go to Bijeljina, to set up contacts with him, and to ensure logistics, because his unit was going into Zvornik and had to be accommodated and put up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us what transpired during the course of that meeting in the Dom culture centre?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: In actual fact, I said who'd sent me. He asked me what the situation was like in Zvornik briefly. And then he called a short man, introduced him as Major Pejic, and told me that he would be leading the group of people assigned to go to Zvornik. This lasted barely two or three minutes. It was a brief meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he indicate who assigned them or Arkan's men to go to Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you see the license plates on the vehicle that Arkan used to arrive at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. He crossed to Karakaj from Mali Zvornik, and the license plates were those of the Federal SUP. I recognised them because they began with a "M" and then a number, and the first number was the number 9, and I knew that was the license plate for the Federal SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So that the record is clear, the time that you saw Arkan in the vehicle was in Zvornik and not Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I saw his vehicle first in Zvornik. I didn't see how he arrived in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: His unit and I with it crossed the Drina River on a ferry at Badovinci, we crossed into Serbia. And then we went to Banja Radalj, which is where there is a hotel. The hotel is about 10 kilometre from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Approximately how many of Arkan's men did you cross from Bijeljina into Serbia with?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It was a small group of about 20 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Were they armed at the time they crossed into Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. They had long-barreled weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And the place that you described yourself as waiting, I believe you said Banja Radalj. Approximately how far in Serbia did you have to travel to get to that location?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: From where we had crossed with the ferry up to Radalj is about 50 to 60 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the course of that trip, both crossing the border into Serbia and driving through Serbia, did you have at any time see uniformed members of the Serbian police during the course of your journey?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No. Because it was already dark, and we drove in the course of night, so I didn't notice any policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived at Banja Radalj?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: They stayed behind and I went on to Zvornik. The next day we had a meeting together, and they informed us that there was a group of Arkan's men, about 20 of them. If a conflict should break out -- and they said that they were there to help the Serb people if a conflict should break out.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: This meeting that you had with them the next day, was that at -- in Banja Radalj or was it somewhere in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: No, it was in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Just one additional question about your observations in Bijeljina: During the time that you were in Bijeljina, did you see a person known as Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I didn't see Mauzer in Bijeljina. I didn't even know that such a person existed at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after the meeting that you had in Banja Radalj with members of Arkan's Tigers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I didn't have a meeting with them in Radalj. I just left them there. They stayed on. And later on Mr. Pejic would come to the Crisis Staff meeting in Zvornik. We never actually had any meeting in Radalj itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what was discussed at the meeting with the Crisis Staff with Mr. Pejic -- or Major Pejic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, when they were put up in Radalj, the next day a conflict broke out in Sapna and several soldiers were killed and discussions were made for defence preparations and a possible clash.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the members of the Crisis Staff that were present when this meeting was held with Major Pejic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: All the members of the Crisis Staff were there from the list, most of them, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after this event that you've described, this -- I believe you described as several soldiers being killed. Did anything happen after the Crisis Staff learned news about that event?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The killing of the soldier happened on the day or the next day, when the sovereignty of Bosnia-Herzegovina was proclaimed. And at the time, that was something that was quite unacceptable to us. So according to Plan B, we set ourselves apart and formed a parallel government in Karakaj at the Alhos factory premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after you establish that parallel government?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, soon afterwards, the incident took place where the negotiations in Mali Zvornik fell through and where a decision was made according to which Zvornik should be occupied, taken over militarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was the decision taken to occupy or take over by military force the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Arkan and Pejic, who led this on his behalf, they ordered the Crisis Staff to launch the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us where -- were you present when that decision was taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Where was that decision taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The decision was taken in the Alhos building, in the office used by the general manager, the director.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And when was it taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: That was -- I think it was the 7th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What happened after that decision was taken? Was there any further discussion about the implementation of that decision?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, various volunteers started arriving, and we were ordered to collect together as much -- as many people as we could from the Territorial Defence. And there was a subsequent decision the next day; I think it was on the 8th of April in the morning, at perhaps 6.00 a.m. Or rather, it was implemented from 6.00 a.m. onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: So the decision was taken on the 7th of April to militarily occupy Zvornik, and the implementation of that decision began at 6.00 the next day, the 8th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: More or less, yes, according to my information. Because I was wounded at the time, and I was at the headquarters in my slippers. I wasn't actually on the ground, in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned volunteers started arriving. From where did the volunteers come?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Mostly from Serbia. I think that some of them were from Bijeljina, because that's the first time I saw the man you mentioned a moment ago, Mr. Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you give us some sense of how many volunteers arrived from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The inflow was quite uncontrolled. And according to my information, more than 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And these volunteers, as you called them, were they associated with any named organisations or groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: According to my information, apart from Arkan's group, the others didn't have groups of their own at that time. There were sporadic cases, individual cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know if when these people arrived in Zvornik, whether they came with their own weapons or whether they were issued weapons once they arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I know that they were issued weapons at the TO headquarters in the Alhos building.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After the decision was taken on the 7th of April, how soon after that did these volunteers begin to arrive in the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, some groups were already in place, ever since the conflict broke out. But within the space of 24 hours or 48 hours, they started coming in in larger numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe to the Chamber how it was that the military takeover of Zvornik occurred.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: What I can tell you is this: I spent the morning at the headquarters. I was injured and I was in my slippers. And you could just hear, because it's very close by, and I received information that the units of the Territorial Defence and the volunteers had occupied Zvornik and placed it under Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: What, if any, involvement or support did the JNA or the Yugoslav People's Army have in the military occupation of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: For this operation itself, I have no information that the JNA took part in the attack itself on that first day against Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time after the first day when the Yugoslav People's Army was involved in the -- in the attack on Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: What I know is this: Later on, some 20 days later, when Kula was taken control of - and that is situated above the hydroelectric power station at Mali Zvornik - is that a unit from Yugoslavia took part in taking control of Kula.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, the people that you've described as volunteers, after the initial takeover of Zvornik did they -- did they begin to form organisations of named groups that you could tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. It is common knowledge that they grouped afterwards, established formations, and the formations took the names of their leaders by and large. And it is also common knowledge that some of them were incorporated into the police and some became a part of TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you tell us the names of these groups or as many of these groups as you can recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I have heard of several, but it was common knowledge that Gogic's unit was in the police. And in the TO there was Zuca's unit, Pivarski's men, Niski's men, the White Eagles, Beli Orlovi, and perhaps some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Zuca's unit, do you know Zuca's full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I read about that in the papers later. I didn't know it at the time, but I know now that his name is Vojin Vuckovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: How were these people that came into Zvornik and participated in the attack on Zvornik, where were they accommodated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: There were different localities. I know that some were put up in Karakaj in some barracks that were empty. Later on, others took over the Muslim houses that had been vacated and left empty. But the TO sorted their accommodation, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was there a bus link established to transport them from Serbia into Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The bus link was never interrupted, because the bus line from Mali Zvornik always operated towards Belgrade and Uzice, because it was the territory that had not been engulfed by the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who was responsible for paying the buses that were transporting these volunteers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I know that the provisional or temporary government paid for the transport vehicles and the ones used to bring in the volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: These people you call "volunteers," were they ever paid money by the municipality for their participation in the takeover of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. They were paid regularly, like all the other members of the TO and the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 5. This is a document encompassing several documents. I'd ask you to review the bundle of documents and ask you: Do you recognise what those documents are?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. It is a document by which the provisional government issues salaries to members of the TO unit that acted within Zuca's unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you to look at the monitor in front of you. There will be one of those documents displayed in front of you, and ask you to read the names after the red bar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I can't see any red markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I draw your attention to number 41 and 44.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I see. Under number 41 is Vuckovic, Vojin, Zuca; and 44 is Vuckovic, Dusko.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Is one of these men the Zuca that you refer to in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, the one under number 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that those documents -- we're finished with those -- but that the witness now be shown Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: While that document is being put before you, you've mentioned Captain Dragan Obrenovic. And my question to you is: Did Captain Obrenovic ever attend meetings of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Captain Dragan Obrenovic did not attend meetings of the Crisis Staff up until the beginning of the war; however, once the war started, while I was a member of the Crisis Staff, he did attend meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And at the time that he attended those meetings, was he still a member of the Yugoslav People's Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Dragan Obrenovic was always a member of the JNA, until the Army of Republika Srpska was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And was he present during meetings in the Crisis Staff when the discussions regarding the implementation of Plan B were held?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, as I was saying, he was present from the beginning of the war up until I was a member of the Crisis Staff, when the discussion centred on the implementation of Plan B.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did he receive payment from the Municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. It can be seen from this document that Dragan Obrenovic did receive a salary as a member of the TO of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did the document you're referring to is Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 6. Could I ask you to describe for us what is that document.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It is the payments for the month of May to Dragan Obrenovic. And the document was approved by Marko Pavlovic on behalf of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: If I can now turn your attention to what you know about the relationship between Arkan and the Yugoslav People's Army as you were able to observe during the takeover of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, the situation was such that all of us who were in the Crisis Staff, including Dragan Obrenovic, who was a JNA officer, would stand to attention when Arkan walked in together with his officer Pejic, who was in command in Zvornik. And there were some other army officers. But we were surprised to see that all of them stood at attention whenever Arkan walked in or out of the room.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did you ever have a conversation with Brano Grujic regarding an incident that occurred between Colonel Milosevic and Arkan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. On one occasion, Grujic said that Arkan had slapped Colonel Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when Arkan left the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. He was in Zvornik twice for an hour or two each time.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: After he left Zvornik, did Marko Pavlovic assume head -- duties of head of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that the witness be shown Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 7. And the usher -- we have three documents to work with in quick succession, so perhaps it might be most convenient to just remain by the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise what is document -- the document Prosecution 451, tab 7? What is that document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. This is the decision to form the command of the Territorial Defence of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik, and Pavlovic is being appointed commander by Grujic as head of the interim government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd ask you: Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what do you recognise that document to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It is the formation of a unified military and territorial command of the Serbian Municipality of Zvornik. And in Article 3, Marko Pavlovic is appointed commander of the military territorial command, and he is appointed to that post by Branko Grujic as head of the interim government.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And finally, I'd ask you to take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 9 and ask you, do you recognise this exhibit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. All these documents were published in the Official Gazette. It is a decision banning taking of food from the compound of the headquarters of the interim government, where in addition to the government only Marko Pavlovic could approve any such taking of food. And this was adopted on the 14th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm finished with those exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Sir, are you aware of a unit called the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When was that unit formed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It was formed, actually, when the Army of Republika Srpska was formed, and that would be, I think, at the end of May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who was the first commander of that unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: There were several commanders. I think it was Blagojevic, then Dragan Petkovic, Bosancic. So in 1992 there were several different commanders that replaced one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Who was the eventual -- was there a commander of that unit that once he became commander remained there for an extended period of time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. From the end of 1992 until the end of the war, the commander of the Zvornik Brigade was Vinko Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've just identified several documents giving Marko Pavlovic authority over the Territorial Defence of Zvornik. How long did his command of the Territorial Defence of Zvornik last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: After Arkan left Zvornik, he took over command of the TO, until he was arrested. I think this was in July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who arrested him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: He was arrested by a special police unit of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And do you know what ultimately happened with that arrest or do you know what charges he was arrested upon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't know that. I just know that he was in detention for only two or three days in the prison in Bijeljina, upon which he was released.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: During the military takeover of Zvornik, were there any Territorial Defence members not from Zvornik but from Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, there were volunteers from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm not just talking about volunteers that you described before. I'm talking about official members of the Territorial Defence or Territorial Defence units in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I am not aware that anyone was an active participant, except the logistic cooperation which we had with the TO staff in Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you take a look at Prosecution Exhibit 251, tab 10. I'd ask you to look at that bundle of documents and ask you: Do you recognise what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. From the documents, we see that these are salaries for the month of April for volunteers from Gogic's unit from Loznica.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And that is Loznica in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, these people you're calling volunteers, would it be fair to say that these are members -- this Bogic's [sic] unit, is this a unit of the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes, Gogic's unit. For a while they were within the police of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Now, in July, in addition to Marko Pavlovic being arrested, were other people arrested in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. Some other unit leaders were arrested as well. I know that Zuca was arrested and his unit, Niski and his unit, and some others.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And who headed the special police unit who arrested them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Milenko Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And why were these people arrested?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Well, because they were causing disturbances in town and they could not longer be kept under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I'm going to ask that you look at Prosecution Exhibit 451, tab 11. And can you tell us, do you recognise this document? And if so, what is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. This is a bill whereby the interim government is paying for the transport of volunteers to a private transporter from Sapot in Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where do those volunteer -- does the receipt indicate where those people were being transported from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. They were transported from Belgrade to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And how much money is reflected in this receipt was due the bus transportation company?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: It says here 80.000 dinars, but there was an inflation and I don't know how realistic that sum is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Are you able to approximate what that -- what the value of 80.000 dinars was in German Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: I don't think anyone could tell now, because there was really a galloping inflation. It's impossible to calculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: You've mentioned Mrs. Plavsic making two visits to Zvornik. I'd ask you to now tell us, when was her second visit to Zvornik during the spring of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: That was two or three days after Serbs had taken control of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And where did she come to, specifically? What building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: She came to the Alhos building, where the Crisis Staff was. And I happened to be the only men present. I was still wearing slippers. I couldn't go out. And with her was Princess Jelisaveta Karadjordjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And what happened after they arrived at the Alhos factory?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: We were waiting for members of the Crisis Staff to arrive, and then we went to have lunch until they arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And during the course of lunch, did you have discussions with her regarding what had taken place in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. I informed her as far as I knew about the situation in Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Zvornik after it was placed under the control of the Serbs of Zvornik, and she enquired as to the extent to which we were implementing the plans, how organised we were. In principle, this was an exchange of information between us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did she provide you with information regarding what was taking place in other municipalities in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: The situation was rather chaotic, so we spoke about everything, but nothing very substantive.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you were together with her that Major Pejic was also present?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes. When we returned to headquarters, I accompanied her to the office of the Crisis Staff. She greeted Pejic. They exchanged warm greetings. And then she held a meeting with a part of the Crisis Staff, but I did not attend that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: When you say she exchanged warm greetings with Mayor Pejic, can you please be more specific?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can you please describe exactly how they greeted each other.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS B-024
utterances.text: They greeted each other in the traditional fashion amongst us Serbs when people know each other really well. We embrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm about to embark on a completely different area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That's a convenient moment. We ought to consider the arrangements for Monday. How much longer do you think you will be with this witness in examination-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: I estimate between 30 and 40 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Effectively that will be about just over two hours. The question is whether the witness who's returning should be interposed first thing. Do you have any views as to that?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. We'll leave it to the Court's discretion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. We will interpose Mr. de la Brosse for the remainder of his cross-examination, which if I recollect rightly is due to last an hour and a half. So that effectively would be the first session. We will then continue with this witness's evidence thereafter. So Mr. Milosevic, when you come on Monday morning, subject to any unforeseen circumstances, Mr. de la Brosse will be here for you to finish your cross-examination, and then we'll go on with this witness. Witness B-024, could you be back, please, on Monday morning, when I hope we'll be able to finish your evidence. We'll adjourn now until then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
